Liberty CTI LLC (“Liberty CTI”) publishes the Alamo Threat Brief™ and related intelligence products for executive, board, and risk-governance audiences. The Terms of Use below govern your use of the Liberty CTI website and the Alamo Threat Brief. The Privacy Policy, which is incorporated into the Terms, explains what information we collect and how we use it.

In short: the Alamo Threat Brief is provided free of charge; our original writing and analysis belong to Liberty CTI, while we claim no ownership of the facts, public-domain material, or third-party reporting we cite; our assessments are analytical judgments under uncertainty, not guarantees, and do not constitute legal, financial, or other professional advice; and these Terms are governed by the laws of the State of Texas. The full documents below set out the details, including limitations, disclaimers, and your rights.

Terms of Use

Nothing in this section is intended to prohibit legitimate quotation, citation, commentary, or other use protected by fair use or an equivalent legal doctrine.

5. Intelligence & Informational-Use Disclaimer

Liberty CTI products provide intelligence analysis and decision support based on information available at the time of publication. Assessments reflect analytical judgments under uncertainty and are not guarantees of future events. The threat landscape changes continuously, and information in any Liberty CTI product may become outdated after publication.

6. No Professional Advice

Liberty CTI provides intelligence analysis and decision support, a discipline distinct from legal, investment, financial, accounting, insurance, or technical cybersecurity implementation services. 8. No Guarantee of Outcomes

Liberty CTI's products are designed to sharpen the quality of your organization’s decisions under uncertainty. They do not guarantee any particular outcome. Specifically, Liberty CTI does not guarantee:

  • The prevention of any security incident;
  • That every relevant threat will be identified;

  • The accuracy of third-party reporting that Liberty CTI cites or relies upon;

Liberty CTI analysis may support risk governance, executive decision-making, due diligence, board deliberation, continuity planning, and regulatory preparation. On its own, however, Liberty CTI analysis does not establish legal compliance, satisfy fiduciary duties, satisfy regulatory obligations, constitute a cybersecurity certification, or create a legal safe harbor.

Part Two

Privacy Policy

1. Information You Provide

Liberty CTI collects information you choose to give us directly, including:

  • Alamo Threat Brief registration: full name, work email address, organization, role/title, and industry sector, plus whether you opt in to receive the free weekly executive summary and Liberty CTI updates.
  • Sign-in: the email address you use to sign back in to a registered account.
  • Contact form: full name, organization, email address, and the content of your message.

We do not currently collect payment information, account passwords, or government identification through the Services.

2. Automatically Collected Information

Liberty CTI does not run third-party analytics or advertising trackers on the website. Beyond the standard server and content-delivery logs generated by our hosting infrastructure (Cloudflare), which may include IP address, browser and device information, and request timestamps for security and reliability purposes, the site does not automatically collect additional behavioral or analytics data about visitors. The site loads typefaces from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address when a page loads.

When you register for Alamo Threat Brief access, our system additionally records the page you registered from and, where provided by your browser, the referring page, as part of the registration record described below.

3. ATB Reader Tracking

Liberty CTI may record when a registered reader's account was created, last used to sign in, and updated, in order to administer Alamo Threat Brief access. We do not record which individual ATB issues a registered reader has opened against their account, and the hosting logs described in Section 2 are not linked to reader accounts, although they may show which pages were requested from an IP address; if Liberty CTI begins recording issue-level readership in the future, this policy will be updated to describe that practice before it takes effect.

4. Purposes of Processing

Liberty CTI uses the information described above to:

  • Administer Alamo Threat Brief reader accounts and grant access to full issues;
  • Respond to inquiries submitted through the contact form;
  • Send the free weekly executive summary and Liberty CTI updates to readers who opt in;
  • Maintain the security, integrity, and reliability of the Services and prevent abuse (for example, the registration form's spam-prevention safeguard); and
  • Understand how readers find the Alamo Threat Brief and improve Liberty CTI’s products.

5. Vendors & Service Providers

Liberty CTI uses a limited number of third-party service providers to operate the Services:

  • Cloudflare: hosting, content delivery, security services, and the Workers KV storage that holds Alamo Threat Brief registration records.
  • Brevo: email delivery for readers who opt in to the weekly executive summary and Liberty CTI updates.
  • Formspree: processing of website contact form submissions.

Each provider processes information only as necessary to perform these functions on Liberty CTI's behalf.

Liberty CTI also maintains pages on Substack, LinkedIn, and X. If you subscribe to or interact with Liberty CTI on those platforms, their own privacy policies govern the information they collect.

6. Cookies & Similar Technologies

Liberty CTI sets one functional cookie: a signed session cookie (lcti_atb_access) that keeps a registered reader signed in to Alamo Threat Brief access for up to 180 days. This cookie is set only after registration or sign-in, is used solely to maintain your session, and is not used for advertising or cross-site tracking. Liberty CTI does not currently use analytics, advertising, or third-party tracking cookies.

Our hosting provider, Cloudflare, may set strictly necessary security cookies to protect the site from automated abuse. These are not used for advertising or tracking.

7. Data Retention

Liberty CTI retains registration and contact information for as long as reasonably necessary to provide the Services, maintain reader accounts, and meet legitimate business and legal needs. Contact form submissions are retained for up to 24 months. Reader accounts with no sign-in activity for 36 months are deleted. Email subscribers who unsubscribe are retained only on a suppression list to honor that request.

8. Data Security

Liberty CTI applies reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational measures designed to protect the information we hold, including signed session cookies set with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes, encrypted connections, and access controls on our hosting infrastructure. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, and Liberty CTI cannot guarantee absolute, "military-grade," or breach-proof security under all circumstances. If a breach affects your personal information, Liberty CTI will notify you as required by Texas law.

9. Your Choices

  • Marketing communications: you may decline the free weekly executive summary and Liberty CTI updates by not opting in at registration. Every email includes an unsubscribe link, and you may also contact Liberty CTI to be removed.
  • Your information: you may ask us to confirm what personal information we hold about you, provide a copy, correct it, or delete it. Email intel@libertycti.com from the address associated with your account. We will respond within 45 days. If you disagree with our response, reply asking us to reconsider, and we will respond within 60 days.
  • General privacy questions: contact Liberty CTI at any time using the details below.

10. Texas Privacy Considerations

Liberty CTI is based in San Antonio, Texas. Liberty CTI is a small business as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration, and our services are designed for professionals acting in a business capacity. We nonetheless extend the choices described in Section 9 to every reader. If you remain unsatisfied after our response to a request for reconsideration, you may contact the Texas Attorney General at texasattorneygeneral.gov. Liberty CTI does not sell personal information, including sensitive personal information, and does not use it for targeted advertising or profiling.

11. Minors

The Services are intended for business and professional users and are not directed to minors. Liberty CTI does not knowingly collect personal information from minors under the age of 18. If we learn that we have collected information from someone under 18, we will delete it.

12. Policy Updates

Liberty CTI may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. The version number and effective date at the top of this page identify the current revision. For material changes, we will notify registered readers by email before they take effect.
